messages:
nate: quick note from onboarding this morning: found three small but painful docs drifts that cause copy/paste failures and SDK surprises for new users.
nate: 1) README Python quickstart still shows `from redwood import Client; client.chat('hi')` which throws since the SDK switched to `responses.create`.
nate: 2) The sample Dockerfile in the sample-app uses ARG REDWOOD_KEY but the quickstart uses REDWOOD_API_KEY; folks building the container ended up with an empty env var at runtime.
nate: 3) Our curl example uses backslash line-continuations which GitHub soft-wraps and sometimes inserts a trailing space; terminals then treat the next line as a new command (support saw a spike in 401s).

sylvia: Ugh. I hit the Python one today: the repo has both async and sync examples, but the async one imports `RedwoodClient` (old class) and calls `await client.chat()`; it needs to be `from redwood import Redwood; client = Redwood(api_key=...) ; await client.responses.create(input='...')`. I'll paste a corrected snippet in a sec.

sylvia: Corrected Python async snippet:

sylvia: ```py
from redwood import Redwood
import os

client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = await client.responses.create(input='Hello from Python')
print(resp.output)
```

mike: For the Dockerfile mismatch: the sample-app Dockerfile uses `ARG REDWOOD_KEY` and `ENV REDWOOD_KEY=$REDWOOD_KEY` but our quickstart docs reference `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. Small rename drift after a refactor. Suggest harmonizing to REDWOOD_API_KEY everywhere and add a short note in the Dockerfile about ARG vs ENV so builders don't accidentally override at runtime.

mike: Also propose we replace the multiline curl with a one-line variant and add explicit Windows cmd and PowerShell examples. One-liner suggestion:

mike: ```
curl -sS --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --header 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses --data-raw '{"input":"hi"}'
```

mike: Windows cmd example:

mike: ```
set REDWOOD_API_KEY=your_key_here
curl -sS --header "Content-Type: application/json" --header "Authorization: Bearer %REDWOOD_API_KEY%" https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses --data-raw "{\"input\":\"hi\"}"
```

mike: PowerShell example:

mike: ```powershell
$body = '{"input":"hi"}'
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses' -Method Post -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY"; 'Content-Type' = 'application/json' } -Body $body
```

nate: Also add a short Troubleshooting note: "If a pasted curl fails, try the one-liner or verify your shell's variable syntax (fish, cmd, PowerShell differ)." Link to a small table of variable syntaxes.

support-bot: Created support tickets: #7010, #7011 referencing several onboarding failures.

docs-bot: Created issue #7020: "docs: fix quickstart example drift - python SDK examples, Dockerfile env var, and curl quoting; add Windows/PowerShell variants" - https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/7020

sylvia: I'll open a tiny PR consolidating the fixes (rename Docker ARG to REDWOOD_API_KEY, update Python snippets to responses.create, swap multiline curl for one-line + PS/cmd examples, add Troubleshooting note). Tagging @mike for Dockerline review.
mike: Happy to review. :thumbsup:
